name: Bobby Farrell
milestone_by_age_26: Was a member of Boney M. when their single 'Daddy Cool' was released on May 31, 1976 and became a European hit after a September 1976 TV appearance, when Farrell was 26 years old.
starting_point: Born in San Nicolaas, Aruba in 1949; left school at 15 to work as a sailor before moving to Norway and then Germany as a DJ and dancer.
current_position: Died on December 30, 2010 at age 61 in Saint Petersburg, Russia, while on tour as Bobby Farrell of Boney M.

trajectory.title: Born in Aruba
trajectory.description: Roberto Alfonso Farrell was born on October 6, 1949, in San Nicolaas, Aruba, a Caribbean island in the Netherlands Antilles.

trajectory.title: Left home as a sailor
trajectory.description: Farrell left school at age 15 to go to sea, working as a sailor for two years before traveling to Norway and then the Netherlands.

trajectory.title: Spotted by Frank Farian
trajectory.description: German producer Frank Farian spotted Farrell working as a DJ in Germany and recruited him as the frontman and dancer for his new disco group Boney M.

trajectory.title: Boney M. breakthrough with 'Daddy Cool'
trajectory.description: Boney M. released 'Daddy Cool' in May 1976; after a September 1976 TV appearance the single became a European hit, launching the group to fame.

trajectory.title: UK #1 with 'Rivers of Babylon'
trajectory.description: Boney M. topped the UK charts with 'Rivers of Babylon'/'Brown Girl in the Ring,' 1978's biggest-selling single, cementing the group as a global disco phenomenon with over 100 million records sold.

trajectory.title: Fired from Boney M.
trajectory.description: Farrell was ousted from Boney M. in 1981 due to clashes with Frank Farian, who confirmed Farrell did not sing on the group's records; he was replaced by Reggie Tsiboe.

trajectory.title: Rejoined Boney M.
trajectory.description: Farrell rejoined Boney M. in 1984 and continued as a member until the group's final split in 1986.

trajectory.title: Boney M. disbands
trajectory.description: Boney M. officially disbanded in 1986, after which Farrell pursued a solo career touring with backing singers as 'Bobby Farrell of Boney M.'

trajectory.title: Died on tour in Russia
trajectory.description: Farrell was found dead in his hotel room in Saint Petersburg, Russia, on December 30, 2010, after failing to answer a wake-up call before a scheduled performance.

name: Marie Fredriksson
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut solo album 'Het vind' on EMI Sweden in September 1984 at age 26, which peaked at number 20 on the Swedish album chart, preceded by the top-20 single 'Ännu doftar kärlek' in May 1984.
starting_point: Born in Össjö, Sweden in 1958; grew up in a small town and moved to Halmstad after graduating from music school in 1977 to work in theatre before entering the indie music scene.
current_position: Died on December 9, 2019 at age 61 in Djursholm, Sweden, after a long battle with a brain tumor; final role was as lead vocalist of Roxette.

trajectory.title: Born in Össjö, Sweden
trajectory.description: Gun-Marie Fredriksson was born on May 30, 1958, in Össjö, Sweden, and grew up in the small town of Östra Ljungby.

trajectory.title: Formed punk band Strul
trajectory.description: Fredriksson formed the punk group Strul in Halmstad, creating their own music festival Strulfestivalen in 1979 which became financially successful.

trajectory.title: Debut solo album 'Het vind'
trajectory.description: Released her debut solo album 'Het vind' on EMI Sweden in September 1984, peaking at #20 on the Swedish album chart, preceded by the top-20 single 'Ännu doftar kärlek'.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Roxette with Per Gessle
trajectory.description: Fredriksson and Per Gessle formed the pop-rock duo Roxette, releasing their debut album 'Pearls of Passion' the same year.

trajectory.title: Roxette's international breakthrough
trajectory.description: Roxette's second album 'Look Sharp!' produced the Billboard Hot 100 #1 hits 'The Look' and 'Listen to Your Heart,' launching them to global stardom.

trajectory.title: 'It Must Have Been Love' and 'Joyride'
trajectory.description: The hit 'It Must Have Been Love' from the Pretty Woman soundtrack reached #1 globally, followed by the album 'Joyride' in 1991 which cemented Roxette as one of the biggest pop acts of the era.

trajectory.title: Diagnosed with brain tumor
trajectory.description: Fredriksson suffered a seizure in September 2002 and was diagnosed with a malignant brain tumor, enduring months of chemotherapy and radiation treatment.

trajectory.title: Died in Djursholm, Sweden
trajectory.description: Fredriksson passed away on December 9, 2019, in Djursholm, Sweden, after a 17-year battle with her brain tumor, leaving behind a legacy as one of Sweden's most beloved vocalists.

name: Andrew Wiles
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored with John Coates the paper 'On the Conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer' (Inventiones Mathematicae, 1977) at age 24, making the first progress on one of mathematics' fundamental conjectures, and became Assistant Professor at Harvard University the same year.
starting_point: Born in Cambridge, England in 1953 to theologian Maurice Frank Wiles and Patricia Wiles; grew up partly in Nigeria where his father was a lecturer, developing an interest in Fermat's Last Theorem at age 10.
current_position: Regius Professor of Mathematics at the University of Oxford; awarded the Abel Prize in 2016 and the Copley Medal in 2017; knighted in 2000.

trajectory.title: Born in Cambridge, England
trajectory.description: Andrew John Wiles was born on April 11, 1953, in Cambridge, England, to theologian Maurice Frank Wiles and Patricia Wiles.

trajectory.title: Discovered Fermat's Last Theorem
trajectory.description: Found a book on Fermat's Last Theorem in his local library and became captivated, declaring 'I knew from that moment that I would never let it go.'

trajectory.title: Graduated from Oxford
trajectory.description: Completed his BA at Merton College, Oxford, before moving to Clare College, Cambridge for graduate studies under John Coates.

trajectory.title: First progress on Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
trajectory.description: Co-authored with John Coates the paper 'On the Conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer' in Inventiones Mathematicae, and became Assistant Professor at Harvard University.

trajectory.title: PhD from Cambridge
trajectory.description: Awarded his PhD from Clare College, Cambridge, for his thesis 'Reciprocity laws and the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer.'

trajectory.title: Professor at Princeton
trajectory.description: Appointed professor at Princeton University, where he would spend the next two decades working on number theory.

trajectory.title: Began secret work on Fermat's Last Theorem
trajectory.description: Upon reading Ken Ribet's work linking Fermat's Last Theorem to the modularity theorem, Wiles set out to prove modularity for semistable elliptic curves in secret.

trajectory.title: Announced proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
trajectory.description: Announced his proof at a series of lectures at Cambridge in June 1993, making international headlines before a flaw was discovered.

trajectory.title: Published corrected proof
trajectory.description: With his student Richard Taylor, Wiles circumvented the flaw and published the complete proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995 to widespread acclaim.

trajectory.title: Awarded the Abel Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Abel Prize, often called the 'Nobel Prize of mathematics,' for his proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.

name: Andrés Escobar
milestone_by_age_26: By age 22, Escobar had debuted for Atlético Nacional's senior team (1986, age 19), helped the club win the 1989 Copa Libertadores—the most prestigious club tournament in South American football—and the 1989 Copa Interamericana, and played at the 1990 FIFA World Cup for Colombia.
starting_point: Born in Medellín, Colombia in 1967 to a middle-class family; grew up playing football and attended Colegio Calasanz before joining Atlético Nacional's youth academy.
current_position: Died on July 2, 1994 at age 27 in Medellín, Colombia, murdered after scoring an own goal in the 1994 FIFA World Cup; final role: defender for Atlético Nacional and the Colombia national team.

trajectory.title: Born in Medellín, Colombia
trajectory.description: Andrés Escobar Saldarriaga was born on March 13, 1967, in Medellín, Colombia, to a middle-class family.

trajectory.title: Debuted for Atlético Nacional
trajectory.description: Escobar made his senior team debut for Atlético Nacional, beginning a career as a centre-back known for clean play and calmness on the pitch.

trajectory.title: Colombia national team debut
trajectory.description: Made his debut for the Colombia national team, beginning an international career that would include 51 caps.

trajectory.title: Won Copa Libertadores with Atlético Nacional
trajectory.description: Helped Atlético Nacional win the 1989 Copa Libertadores, the most prestigious club tournament in South American football, and the 1989 Copa Interamericana.

trajectory.title: Played at 1990 FIFA World Cup
trajectory.description: Represented Colombia at the 1990 FIFA World Cup in Italy, where the team reached the Round of 16; also had a brief spell with Swiss club BSC Young Boys.

trajectory.title: Won Colombian league title
trajectory.description: Won the Colombian league title with Atlético Nacional, establishing himself as one of the country's most admired defenders, nicknamed 'The Gentleman of Football.'

trajectory.title: Own goal at 1994 World Cup and murder
trajectory.description: Scored an own goal in Colombia's 2-1 defeat to the United States at the 1994 World Cup on June 22; ten days later on July 2, he was shot dead outside a bar in Medellín, reportedly in retaliation for the own goal.

name: Gene Simmons
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the rock band KISS in January 1973 at age 23, releasing three studio albums by age 26 including the debut 'Kiss' (Feb 1974) and 'Dressed to Kill' (Mar 1975).
starting_point: Born Chaim Witz on August 25, 1949, in Haifa, Israel; immigrated to New York City with his mother as a child, changed name to Gene Klein, and played in several bands as a teenager.
current_position: Co-founder and bassist of KISS; net worth estimated at ~$400 million; resides in Los Angeles; KISS retired from touring in 2023.

trajectory.title: Born in Haifa, Israel
trajectory.description: Born Chaim Witz on August 25, 1949, in Haifa, Israel, to a carpenter father and Holocaust survivor mother Florence Klein.

trajectory.title: Immigrated to the United States
trajectory.description: Moved to New York City with his mother, changed his name to Gene Klein, and discovered comic books and rock and roll.

trajectory.title: First band: The Missing Links
trajectory.description: Formed his first band, Lynx, later renamed the Missing Links, beginning a teenage obsession with playing guitar and performing.

trajectory.title: Formed Wicked Lester with Paul Stanley
trajectory.description: Met Stanley Eisen (Paul Stanley) and formed Wicked Lester, recording an album that was never released by Epic Records.

trajectory.title: Co-founded KISS
trajectory.description: Abandoned Wicked Lester and co-founded KISS with Paul Stanley, Ace Frehley, and Peter Criss in January 1973, adopting the 'Demon' persona.

trajectory.title: Released debut album 'Kiss'
trajectory.description: KISS released their self-titled debut album in February 1974, establishing their shock rock style with face paint and elaborate stage performances.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough album 'Destroyer'
trajectory.description: Released 'Destroyer' in March 1976, featuring the hit 'Beth' and cementing KISS as one of the top hard rock acts of the 1970s.

trajectory.title: KISS removes makeup
trajectory.description: KISS shed their signature makeup in 1983, experiencing a commercial resurgence with the album 'Lick It Up.'

trajectory.title: Inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: KISS was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014 as one of the most influential hard rock bands in history.

trajectory.title: KISS retired from touring
trajectory.description: KISS completed their End of the Road farewell tour in December 2023, with Simmons and Stanley as the only constant members throughout the band's 50-year history.

name: Anna Netrebko
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Mikhail Glinka vocal competition in 1993 at age 22 and made her operatic stage debut at the Mariinsky Theatre in 1994 at age 22 as Susanna in The Marriage of Figaro, followed by her US debut at San Francisco Opera in 1995 and entry into the Merola Opera Program in 1996.
starting_point: Born in Krasnodar, Russia in 1971 to a geologist father and communications engineer mother; moved to Leningrad at 16 to study at the St. Petersburg Conservatory while working as a janitor at the Mariinsky Theatre.
current_position: One of the world's leading operatic sopranos; continues to perform at major opera houses globally; an exclusive Deutsche Grammophon recording artist since 2003.

trajectory.title: Born in Krasnodar, Russia
trajectory.description: Anna Yuryevna Netrebko was born on September 18, 1971, in Krasnodar, Russia, to a family of Kuban Cossack background.

trajectory.title: Entered St. Petersburg Conservatory
trajectory.description: Moved to Leningrad and entered the St. Petersburg State Conservatory while working as a janitor at the Mariinsky Theatre to watch rehearsals for free.

trajectory.title: Won Mikhail Glinka vocal competition
trajectory.description: Won first prize at the 15th International Glinka Competition of Vocalists in Smolensk, launching her professional career.

trajectory.title: Operatic debut at Mariinsky Theatre
trajectory.description: Made her operatic stage debut at the Mariinsky Theatre as Susanna in The Marriage of Figaro, under the guidance of conductor Valery Gergiev.

trajectory.title: US debut at San Francisco Opera
trajectory.description: Made her American debut as Lyudmila in Glinka's Ruslan and Lyudmila at the San Francisco Opera, followed by enrollment in the Merola Opera Program in 1996.

trajectory.title: Salzburg Festival breakthrough
trajectory.description: Performed Donna Anna in Mozart's Don Giovanni at the 2002 Salzburg Festival, gaining global recognition and leading to an exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon.

trajectory.title: Signed with Deutsche Grammophon
trajectory.description: Signed an exclusive recording contract with Deutsche Grammophon and released her first solo album 'Anna Netrebko – Opera Arias.'

trajectory.title: Named to Time 100 most influential people
trajectory.description: Became the first classical music artist named to Time magazine's annual list of the world's 100 most influential people.

trajectory.title: Continuing international career
trajectory.description: Continues to headline productions at the world's leading opera houses, with upcoming role debuts including Strauss' Ariadne auf Naxos and Tchaikovsky's Pique Dame.

name: Addison Rae
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with talent agency WME in January 2020 at age 19, joined The Hype House in December 2019, amassed 88M+ TikTok followers, and was one of the highest-earning TikTok personalities by 2020, later releasing her debut single 'Obsessed' (2021) and starring in Netflix's 'He's All That' (2021).
starting_point: Born Addison Rae Easterling on October 6, 2000, in Lafayette, Louisiana; began competitive dance training at age 6 and briefly attended LSU for broadcast journalism before dropping out to pursue TikTok fame.
current_position: Pop singer and actress with 88M+ TikTok followers; released debut album 'Addison' in 2025; Grammy-nominated for Best New Artist in 2026; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Born in Lafayette, Louisiana
trajectory.description: Addison Rae Easterling was born on October 6, 2000, in Lafayette, Louisiana, and began competitive dance training at age six.

trajectory.title: Joined TikTok and The Hype House
trajectory.description: Joined TikTok in July 2019 posting dance videos, joined The Hype House collective in December 2019, and quickly amassed over one million followers.

trajectory.title: Signed with WME and highest-earning TikTok star
trajectory.description: Signed with talent agency WME in January 2020; was ranked the highest-earning TikTok personality by Forbes in August 2020 with over 88 million followers.

trajectory.title: Debut single 'Obsessed' and Netflix film
trajectory.description: Released her debut single 'Obsessed' in March 2021 and starred in the Netflix film 'He's All That,' a gender-bending remake of the 1999 teen classic.

trajectory.title: Debut EP 'AR' and Atlantic Records deal
trajectory.description: Signed a publishing deal with Atlantic Records and released her debut self-titled EP 'AR' in August 2023, marking her transition from social media star to pop artist.

trajectory.title: Breakout single 'Diet Pepsi'
trajectory.description: Released 'Diet Pepsi' which peaked at #54 on the Billboard Hot 100 and amassed nearly 400 million Spotify streams, her first Billboard Hot 100 hit.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Addison' and Grammy nomination
trajectory.description: Released her debut album 'Addison' to critical acclaim and was nominated for Grammy Best New Artist in 2026, cementing her transition from TikTok star to legitimate pop artist.

name: Bella Poarch
milestone_by_age_26: Created the most-liked video on TikTok in August 2020 at age 23 (a lip-sync to Millie B's 'M to the B' with 56M+ likes), signed with Warner Records in 2021, and released debut single 'Build a Bitch' which charted at #56 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the most-watched music video on YouTube in its first 24 hours.
starting_point: Born Belinda Marie Macadengdeng Batumbakal on February 9, 1997, in the Philippines; raised by her grandmother until age 3, then adopted by an American military veteran and his Filipino wife; experienced childhood abuse before enlisting in the US Navy.
current_position: Singer and social media personality with 93M+ TikTok followers; signed to Warner Records; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Born in the Philippines
trajectory.description: Born Belinda Marie Macadengdeng Batumbakal on February 9, 1997, in Pangasinan, Philippines; raised by her grandmother in slums until age 3, then adopted.

trajectory.title: Enlisted in US Navy
trajectory.description: Enlisted in the US Navy as an aviation ordnanceman, serving for three years and stationed in Japan and Hawaii.

trajectory.title: Most-liked TikTok video ever
trajectory.description: Created the most-liked video in TikTok history in August 2020, a lip-sync to Millie B's 'M to the B' that garnered over 56 million likes.

trajectory.title: Signed with Warner Records and 'Build a Bitch'
trajectory.description: Signed with Warner Records in May 2021 and released debut single 'Build a Bitch,' which peaked at #56 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the most-watched music video on YouTube in its first 24 hours.

trajectory.title: Debut EP 'Dolls' and Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Released her debut EP 'Dolls' in August 2022 and was included on Forbes 30 Under 30, solidifying her crossover from social media to music.

trajectory.title: Continuing music and social media career
trajectory.description: Continues as one of the most-followed TikTok creators with over 93 million followers while developing her music career with Warner Records.

name: Loren Gray
milestone_by_age_26: Signed a record deal with Virgin Records in March 2018 at age 15, released debut single 'My Story' in August 2018, and was the most-followed person on TikTok from March 2019 to March 2020 with 50M+ followers, earning $2.4 million in 2019 per Forbes.
starting_point: Born Loren Gray Beech on April 19, 2002, in Pottstown, Pennsylvania; joined Musical.ly (later TikTok) in 2015 at age 13 and moved to Los Angeles after gaining a large following.
current_position: Independent singer-songwriter with 50M+ TikTok followers; released debut album 'Guilty' in 2023; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Born in Pottstown, Pennsylvania
trajectory.description: Loren Gray Beech was born on April 19, 2002, in Pottstown, Pennsylvania.

trajectory.title: Joined Musical.ly (TikTok)
trajectory.description: Joined Musical.ly in 2015, gaining a large following in 8th grade and eventually moving to Los Angeles to pursue a career in entertainment.

trajectory.title: Signed with Virgin Records
trajectory.description: Signed a record deal with Virgin Records in March 2018 and released debut single 'My Story' in August, followed by 'Kick You Out' and 'Queen' before year's end.

trajectory.title: Most-followed on TikTok
trajectory.description: Became the most-followed person on TikTok from March 2019 to March 2020 with over 50 million followers; earned $2.4 million in 2019 per Forbes, making her the fourth highest-earning TikTok star.

trajectory.title: Became independent artist
trajectory.description: Parted ways with Virgin Records in February 2021 and became an independent artist, releasing 'Piece of Work' as her first independent single.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Guilty'
trajectory.description: Released her debut album 'Guilty' in 2023, showcasing her evolution from TikTok star to fully realized pop artist with over 80 million streams on 'Queen' alone.

trajectory.title: Continuing music and content career
trajectory.description: Continues to create music and content with over 50 million TikTok followers and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30, maintaining her status as one of the most influential creators of her generation.

name: Maggie Rogers
milestone_by_age_26: Her song 'Alaska' went viral in 2016 at age 22 after a video of Pharrell Williams's visibly moved reaction during a master class at NYU gained millions of views, leading to a major label deal; her debut album 'Heard It in a Past Life' debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 in January 2019, and she was nominated for Grammy Best New Artist in 2020.
starting_point: Born Margaret Debay Rogers on April 25, 1994, in Easton, Maryland; began playing harp at age 7, studied at the Clive Davis Institute at NYU Tisch School of the Arts.
current_position: Singer-songwriter and record producer; released third album 'Don't Forget Me' in 2024; holds a master's from Harvard Divinity School; resides in New York.

trajectory.title: Born in Easton, Maryland
trajectory.description: Margaret Debay Rogers was born on April 25, 1994, in Easton, Maryland, and began playing harp at age seven.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at NYU Clive Davis Institute
trajectory.description: Enrolled at the Clive Davis Institute of Recorded Music at NYU Tisch School of the Arts, having self-released her first album 'The Echo' during her senior year of high school.

trajectory.title: 'Alaska' goes viral
trajectory.description: Her song 'Alaska' went viral after a video of Pharrell Williams's visibly moved reaction during an NYU master class gained millions of views, leading to a major label deal with Capitol Records.

trajectory.title: Debut album debuted at #2 on Billboard 200
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'Heard It in a Past Life' in January 2019, which debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 and earned widespread critical acclaim.

trajectory.title: Grammy nomination for Best New Artist
trajectory.description: Nominated for Grammy Best New Artist at the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards, cementing her status as a major pop artist.

trajectory.title: Second album 'Surrender' and Harvard master's
trajectory.description: Released second album 'Surrender' in 2022 after graduating from Harvard Divinity School with a Master of Religion and Public Life degree.

trajectory.title: Third album 'Don't Forget Me'
trajectory.description: Released her third studio album 'Don't Forget Me' in 2024, continuing her evolution as a singer-songwriter and producer.

name: Lewis Capaldi
milestone_by_age_26: His single 'Someone You Loved' topped the UK Singles Chart for seven weeks in March 2019 at age 22, reached #1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in November 2019, and his debut album 'Divinely Uninspired to a Hellish Extent' was the best-selling UK album of 2019 and 2020; he won the 2020 Brit Awards for Song of the Year and Best New Artist.
starting_point: Born Lewis Marc Capaldi on October 7, 1996, in Bathgate, Scotland; discovered by his manager through a SoundCloud recording made in his bedroom at age 18; graduated with an HND in Music from New College Lanarkshire.
current_position: Scottish singer-songwriter; returned from hiatus in 2025 with a surprise Glastonbury performance and new single 'Survive'; resides in Scotland.

trajectory.title: Born in Bathgate, Scotland
trajectory.description: Lewis Marc Capaldi was born on October 7, 1996, in Bathgate, Scotland.

trajectory.title: Discovered via SoundCloud
trajectory.description: His manager Ryan Walter discovered him through an iPhone recording uploaded to SoundCloud; Walter flew from the US to Britain the next day to hear Capaldi play live.

trajectory.title: Debut single 'Bruises'
trajectory.description: Released his first single 'Bruises' independently on March 31, 2017, becoming the fastest-ever unsigned artist to reach 25 million plays on Spotify.

trajectory.title: 'Someone You Loved' tops UK and US charts
trajectory.description: 'Someone You Loved' topped the UK Singles Chart for seven weeks in March 2019 and reached #1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in November 2019; debut album was the best-selling UK album of 2019 and 2020.

trajectory.title: Brit Awards wins
trajectory.description: Won the 2020 Brit Awards for Song of the Year and Best New Artist; 'Someone You Loved' became the UK's most streamed song of all time.

trajectory.title: Second album and health hiatus
trajectory.description: Released second album 'Broken by Desire to Be Heavenly Sent' in 2023, supported by the lead single 'Forget Me,' before taking a hiatus due to health issues including Tourette's syndrome.

trajectory.title: Surprise Glastonbury return
trajectory.description: Returned from hiatus with a surprise Glastonbury performance in summer 2025, debuting new single 'Survive' which scored the biggest opening week of his career.

name: Rod Wave
milestone_by_age_26: His single 'Heart on Ice' went viral on TikTok and peaked at #25 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2019 at age 21; debut album 'Ghetto Gospel' peaked at #10 on the Billboard 200 in November 2019; and second album 'Pray 4 Love' peaked at #2 on the Billboard 200 in April 2020, with 'Rags2Riches' reaching #12 on the Hot 100.
starting_point: Born Rodarius Marcell Green on August 27, 1998, in St. Petersburg, Florida; began recording as a pastime facilitated by his father who bought him a microphone and his brother who gave him a computer.
current_position: American rapper and singer; has released six studio albums with three consecutive #1 debuts on the Billboard 200; signed to Alamo Records; resides in Florida.

trajectory.title: Born in St. Petersburg, Florida
trajectory.description: Rodarius Marcell Green was born on August 27, 1998, in St. Petersburg, Florida.

trajectory.title: First mixtape 'Hunger Games Vol. 1'
trajectory.description: Released his first mixtape 'Hunger Games Vol. 1' in 2016, beginning a prolific series of mixtapes that built a local following.

trajectory.title: Signed to Alamo Records
trajectory.description: Signed with Alamo Records and released multiple mixtapes including 'Hunger Games 2' and 'Hunger Games 3' and 'PTSD' in 2018-2019.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'Heart on Ice' and 'Ghetto Gospel'
trajectory.description: 'Heart on Ice' went viral on TikTok and peaked at #25 on the Billboard Hot 100; debut album 'Ghetto Gospel' executive-produced by Kevin Gates peaked at #10 on the Billboard 200.

trajectory.title: 'Pray 4 Love' peaks at #2
trajectory.description: Second album 'Pray 4 Love' debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 with 'Rags2Riches' reaching #12 on the Hot 100; signed a global publishing deal with Sony Music Publishing.

trajectory.title: First #1 album 'SoulFly'
trajectory.description: Third album 'SoulFly' debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200, his first chart-topping album, spawning top-20 singles 'Street Runner' and 'Tombstone'.

trajectory.title: Third consecutive #1 album 'Nostalgia'
trajectory.description: Fifth album 'Nostalgia' debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200, making him the only artist besides Taylor Swift to debut a chart-topping solo album each year from 2021 to 2023.

trajectory.title: Sixth album 'Last Lap'
trajectory.description: Released sixth album 'Last Lap' which debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200, marking his seventh consecutive top-ten album and the only male artist with a top-ten album each year from 2019 to 2024.

name: Rashid Khan
milestone_by_age_26: Made ODI debut for Afghanistan at age 17 in October 2015; became the youngest captain in international cricket history at 19, and the fastest bowler to 100 ODI wickets (44 matches) by age 19 in March 2018.
starting_point: Born on September 20, 1998, in Nangarhar, Afghanistan; grew up in a Pashtun family and spent early years in a refugee camp in Peshawar, Pakistan; developed a passion for cricket watching Shahid Afridi.
current_position: Afghanistan T20I captain and one of the world's leading T20 bowlers; plays for Gujarat Titans in the IPL, Adelaide Strikers in the BBL, and multiple global franchise leagues.

trajectory.title: Born in Nangarhar, Afghanistan
trajectory.description: Rashid Khan Arman was born on September 20, 1998, in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, into a Pashtun family; spent early years in a refugee camp in Peshawar.

trajectory.title: ODI debut for Afghanistan
trajectory.description: Made his ODI debut for Afghanistan against Zimbabwe in October 2015 at age 17, beginning a meteoric rise in international cricket.

trajectory.title: IPL debut with Sunrisers Hyderabad
trajectory.description: Fetched the highest IPL bid for any Associate nation player ever, bought by Sunrisers Hyderabad for INR 4 crore at the 2017 auction; became a vital cog in their lineup.

trajectory.title: Youngest international captain and fastest to 100 ODI wickets
trajectory.description: Became the youngest captain in international cricket history at 19, and the fastest bowler to 100 ODI wickets in just 44 matches in March 2018.

trajectory.title: Test debut and ICC Associate Cricketer of the Year
trajectory.description: Played in Afghanistan's first-ever Test match against India in June 2018; named ICC Associate Cricketer of the Year for 2018.

trajectory.title: T20I captain and Cricket World Cup
trajectory.description: Appointed T20I captain of Afghanistan in April 2019; played in the 2019 Cricket World Cup, reaching his 100th international match during the tournament.

trajectory.title: Fastest to 100 T20I wickets
trajectory.description: Became the fastest bowler in terms of matches to take 100 wickets in T20I cricket, achieving the milestone in his 53rd match in October 2021.

trajectory.title: Joined Gujarat Titans in IPL
trajectory.description: Joined Gujarat Titans in the IPL, continuing his dominance as one of the most sought-after T20 bowlers in global franchise cricket.

trajectory.title: Continuing as Afghanistan's cricket icon
trajectory.description: Continues as Afghanistan's T20I captain and one of the greatest T20 bowlers in the world, playing across multiple global franchise leagues including the IPL, BBL, and PSL.

name: Peter Scholze
milestone_by_age_26: At age 22, redid the 288-page Harris-Taylor proof in 37 pages, stunning the number theory community; at 24, became Germany's youngest full professor after introducing perfectoid spaces in his PhD thesis.
starting_point: Born on December 11, 1987, in Dresden, East Germany; showed extraordinary mathematical talent as a student at the University of Bonn.
current_position: Professor at the University of Bonn and co-director at the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics; Fields Medalist (2018); one of the leading mathematicians in the world.

trajectory.title: Born in Dresden, East Germany
trajectory.description: Peter Scholze was born on December 11, 1987, in Dresden, East Germany.

trajectory.title: Redid Harris-Taylor proof in 37 pages
trajectory.description: As a graduate student at the University of Bonn, redid the 288-page Harris-Taylor proof in only 37 pages, stunning the number theory community.

trajectory.title: Introduced perfectoid spaces
trajectory.description: First described the concept of perfectoid spaces at a 2011 conference as a doctoral student, setting off a revolution in algebraic and arithmetic geometry.

trajectory.title: Germany's youngest full professor
trajectory.description: Made full professor at the University of Bonn shortly after completing his PhD, becoming the youngest full professor in Germany at age 24.

trajectory.title: SASTRA Ramanujan Prize
trajectory.description: Awarded the SASTRA Ramanujan Prize for his contributions to arithmetic geometry and the theory of perfectoid spaces.

trajectory.title: Cole Prize and Fermat Prize
trajectory.description: Won the Cole Prize in Algebra from the AMS and the Fermat Prize for his transformative work in arithmetic geometry.

trajectory.title: Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Rio de Janeiro, the highest honor in mathematics, for revolutionizing arithmetic geometry.

trajectory.title: Co-director at Max Planck Institute
trajectory.description: Appointed as a director at the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in Bonn, while maintaining his Hausdorff Chair at the University of Bonn.

trajectory.title: Elected to the Royal Society
trajectory.description: Elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2022, recognized as the leading mathematician of his generation.

name: Lee Sang-hyeok
milestone_by_age_26: Won the League of Legends World Championship in 2013 at age 17 with SK Telecom T1, and went on to win five more World Championships by age 26, becoming the most decorated LoL player in history.
starting_point: Born Lee Sang-hyeok on May 7, 1996, in Seoul, South Korea; began playing League of Legends under the name 'gojeonpa' and climbed to the top of the Korean ladder as a teenager.
current_position: Mid-laner for T1 (formerly SK Telecom T1); six-time World Champion; first inductee into Riot Games' Hall of Legends (2024); widely regarded as the greatest LoL player of all time.

trajectory.title: Born in Seoul, South Korea
trajectory.description: Lee Sang-hyeok was born on May 7, 1996, in Seoul, South Korea.

trajectory.title: Ranked #1 on Korean ladder
trajectory.description: Playing under the name 'gojeonpa,' climbed to the top of the Korean League of Legends ranked ladder, attracting attention from professional teams.

trajectory.title: First World Championship with SK Telecom T1
trajectory.description: Signed with SK Telecom T1 in February 2013 and won the Season 3 World Championship, defeating Royal Club 3-0 in the grand finals, becoming a star at age 17.

trajectory.title: Second World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his second World Championship with SK Telecom T1, defeating KOO Tigers 3-1 in the finals.

trajectory.title: Third World Championship and first MSI title
trajectory.description: Won his third World Championship and first Mid-Season Invitational title with SKT, cementing his status as the dominant player in LoL history.

trajectory.title: Second MSI title
trajectory.description: Won his second Mid-Season Invitational title with SK Telecom T1, further extending his record as the most decorated LoL player.

trajectory.title: T1 rebrand and continued dominance
trajectory.description: SK Telecom T1 rebranded to T1 in November 2019; Faker continued as the team's mid-laner, the only constant member throughout the organization's history.

trajectory.title: Asian Games gold medal
trajectory.description: Won a gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou representing South Korea in League of Legends, adding to his legacy as the greatest esports player.

trajectory.title: Fourth World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his fourth World Championship with T1, defeating Weibo Gaming 3-0 in the finals, extending his record for most World Championship titles.

trajectory.title: Hall of Legends inductee and fifth World Championship
trajectory.description: Became the first inductee into Riot Games' Hall of Legends in 2024 and won his fifth World Championship with T1.

trajectory.title: Sixth World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his record sixth World Championship with T1 in 2025, further solidifying his status as the undisputed greatest League of Legends player of all time.

name: Jon Jones
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest UFC champion in history at age 23 by defeating Shogun Rua for the UFC Light Heavyweight Championship at UFC 128 on March 19, 2011.
starting_point: Born Jonathan Dwight Jones on July 19, 1987, in Rochester, New York; grew up in a family of athletes with brothers Arthur (NFL) and Chandler (NFL); began MMA training and debuted professionally in 2008.
current_position: Retired from MMA in 2025; former UFC Heavyweight and Light Heavyweight Champion; regarded as one of the greatest mixed martial artists of all time.

trajectory.title: Born in Rochester, New York
trajectory.description: Jonathan Dwight Jones was born on July 19, 1987, in Rochester, New York; brothers Arthur and Chandler both played in the NFL.

trajectory.title: Professional MMA debut
trajectory.description: Made his professional MMA debut in July 2008, winning his first fight; signed with the UFC later that year.

trajectory.title: Youngest UFC champion in history
trajectory.description: Defeated Maurício 'Shogun' Rua at UFC 128 on March 19, 2011, to win the UFC Light Heavyweight Championship, becoming the youngest champion in UFC history.

trajectory.title: Record-tying title defenses
trajectory.description: Defended his light heavyweight title against Chael Sonnen at UFC 159 in April 2013, tying Tito Ortiz's record for most UFC light heavyweight title defenses.

trajectory.title: Stripped of title after hit-and-run
trajectory.description: Was stripped of the light heavyweight title and removed from UFC rankings in 2015 after being arrested on felony hit-and-run charges.

trajectory.title: Reclaimed light heavyweight title
trajectory.description: Returned to the UFC and reclaimed the light heavyweight championship by defeating Alexander Gustafsson at UFC 232 in December 2018.

trajectory.title: Won UFC Heavyweight Championship
trajectory.description: Moved up to heavyweight and won the vacant UFC Heavyweight Championship by submitting Ciryl Gane at UFC 285 in March 2023.

trajectory.title: Defended heavyweight title against Miocic
trajectory.description: Defended the heavyweight title by stopping Stipe Miocic via TKO at UFC 309 in November 2024.

trajectory.title: Retired from MMA
trajectory.description: Vacated the heavyweight title and retired from professional MMA in June 2025, ending a career widely regarded as the greatest in UFC history.

name: Ronda Rousey
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Championship at age 25 in March 2012, then became the inaugural UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion later that year.
starting_point: Born Ronda Jean Rousey on February 1, 1987, in Riverside County, California; began judo at age 11 with her mother, qualified for the 2004 Olympics at 17, and won Olympic bronze in judo at the 2008 Beijing Games.
current_position: Retired from MMA and WWE; actress and author; resides in the United States; inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2018.

trajectory.title: Born in Riverside County, California
trajectory.description: Ronda Jean Rousey was born on February 1, 1987, in Riverside County, California; her mother was a judo world champion.

trajectory.title: Youngest judoka to qualify for Olympics
trajectory.description: Became the youngest judoka to qualify for the 2004 Olympic Games in Athens at age 17; also won gold at the World Judo Juniors Championships.

trajectory.title: Olympic bronze medal in judo
trajectory.description: Won bronze at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first American woman to win an Olympic medal in judo; retired from judo at 21.

trajectory.title: Amateur MMA debut
trajectory.description: Made her amateur MMA debut in August 2010, winning by armbar in 23 seconds; turned professional in March 2011.

trajectory.title: Strikeforce and UFC champion
trajectory.description: Won the Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Championship in March 2012 by defeating Miesha Tate; became the first female fighter signed by the UFC and was named inaugural UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion in November 2012.

trajectory.title: First women's bout in UFC history
trajectory.description: Headlined UFC 157 in February 2013, the first women's bout in UFC history, defeating Liz Carmouche by armbar in the first round.

trajectory.title: First career loss to Holly Holm
trajectory.description: Suffered her first MMA loss at UFC 193 in November 2015, knocked out by Holly Holm, ending her dominant reign as UFC champion.

trajectory.title: Retired from MMA
trajectory.description: Lost to Amanda Nunes at UFC 207 in December 2016 and retired from MMA; was the first female fighter inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2018.

trajectory.title: WWE debut and championship
trajectory.description: Transitioned to professional wrestling, debuting at WWE WrestleMania 34 in 2018 and becoming a three-time WWE Women's Champion.

name: Chloe Kim
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in snowboard halfpipe at age 17 at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics, becoming the youngest woman to win an Olympic snowboarding gold medal.
starting_point: Born on April 23, 2000, in Torrance, California, to Korean immigrant parents; began snowboarding at age 4 at Mountain High resort in Southern California.
current_position: Two-time Olympic gold medalist and eight-time X Games gold medalist; won silver at the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympics; professional snowboarder.

trajectory.title: Born in Torrance, California
trajectory.description: Chloe Kim was born on April 23, 2000, in Torrance, California, to South Korean immigrant parents; began snowboarding at age four.

trajectory.title: Youngest X Games gold medalist
trajectory.description: Became the youngest ever winner of a gold medal at the Winter X Games in 2015 at age 14, taking the superpipe title.

trajectory.title: Youth Olympic double gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in both halfpipe and slopestyle at the 2016 Winter Youth Olympic Games in Lillehammer, becoming the first American woman to win snowboarding gold at the Youth Olympics.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold at Pyeongchang
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in women's snowboard halfpipe at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics at age 17, becoming the youngest woman to win an Olympic snowboarding gold medal with a score of 98.25.

trajectory.title: World Championship gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the 2019 FIS World Championships in Utah, becoming the first snowboarder to win all four major titles: Olympics, Worlds, Youth Olympics, and X Games.

trajectory.title: Second consecutive Olympic gold
trajectory.description: Won her second consecutive Olympic gold medal in halfpipe at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, becoming the first woman to win back-to-back halfpipe golds.

trajectory.title: World Championship and X Games gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the 2025 FIS World Championships in Engadin and X Games gold in Aspen, bringing her total to eight X Games gold medals.

trajectory.title: Olympic silver at Milano Cortina
trajectory.description: Won a silver medal in halfpipe at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympic Games, narrowly missing a historic third consecutive gold.

name: Marc Márquez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 125cc World Championship at age 17 in 2010, then became the youngest MotoGP World Champion in history at age 20 as a rookie in 2013, winning six races in his debut season.
starting_point: Born on February 17, 1993, in Cervera, Spain; began motorcycle racing as a child, joining the World Championship in 2008 at age 15 with backing from Repsol.
current_position: Seven-time MotoGP World Champion (2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2025); rides for the Ducati Lenovo Team; widely considered one of the greatest motorcycle racers of all time.

trajectory.title: Born in Cervera, Spain
trajectory.description: Marc Márquez Alentà was born on February 17, 1993, in Cervera, Spain.

trajectory.title: World Championship debut in 125cc
trajectory.description: Joined the World Speed Championship in 2008 at age 15, contesting 13 grands prix in his first year and achieving a podium at the British Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: 125cc World Champion
trajectory.description: Won the 125cc World Championship in 2010 at age 17, securing his first world title with 10 race wins.

trajectory.title: Moto2 World Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Moto2 World Championship in 2012, establishing himself as a rising star destined for MotoGP.

trajectory.title: Youngest MotoGP World Champion
trajectory.description: Became the youngest MotoGP World Champion in history as a rookie in 2013, winning six races and becoming the first rookie champion in 35 years.

trajectory.title: Dominant second MotoGP title
trajectory.description: Defended his MotoGP title dominantly in 2014, winning the first ten races of the season back-to-back.

trajectory.title: Third MotoGP title
trajectory.description: Won his third MotoGP World Championship in 2016, equaling the all-time Grand Prix record for pole positions.

trajectory.title: Sixth MotoGP title
trajectory.description: Won his sixth MotoGP World Championship in 2019 with a particularly dominant season, becoming the youngest rider to win his eighth Grand Prix championship.

trajectory.title: Career-threatening injury
trajectory.description: Crashed and broke his right humerus at the 2020 season opener in Jerez; underwent multiple surgeries and sat out the entire season, threatening his career.

trajectory.title: Left Honda for Gresini Ducati
trajectory.description: Severed his contract with Honda in 2023 after 11 years and six titles, joining the satellite Gresini Ducati team for 2024 to rebuild his career.

trajectory.title: Seventh MotoGP World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his seventh MotoGP World Championship in 2025 with the Ducati Lenovo Team, completing one of the greatest comebacks in motorsport history.

name: Hayden Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Created and launched Uniswap, a decentralized exchange protocol on Ethereum, deploying it to the Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 at age 26, which became one of the most important protocols in DeFi.
starting_point: Born in 1992; graduated from Stony Brook University with a bachelor's in engineering in 2016; worked as a mechanical engineer at Siemens before being laid off in July 2017.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Uniswap Labs; Uniswap is one of the largest decentralized applications on Ethereum, processing billions in daily trading volume.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stony Brook University
trajectory.description: Graduated with a bachelor's degree in engineering from Stony Brook University and began working as a mechanical engineer at Siemens.

trajectory.title: Laid off from Siemens and discovered Ethereum
trajectory.description: Was laid off from Siemens in July 2017; friend Karl Floersch convinced him to learn Ethereum, Solidity, and JavaScript, beginning his crypto journey.

trajectory.title: Built Uniswap proof-of-concept
trajectory.description: At Karl's suggestion, implemented an automated market maker as described by Vitalik Buterin, building a proof-of-concept from October to November 2017.

trajectory.title: Launched Uniswap on Ethereum mainnet
trajectory.description: Deployed Uniswap to the Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018, publicly announcing it to his ~200 Twitter followers, creating one of the most important protocols in DeFi.

trajectory.title: Uniswap V2 launch and UNI token airdrop
trajectory.description: Launched Uniswap V2 in 2020 and the UNI token via airdrop in September 2020; Uniswap surpassed Coinbase Pro in daily trading volume for the first time.

trajectory.title: Uniswap V3 launch
trajectory.description: Launched Uniswap V3 in May 2021, introducing concentrated liquidity, making it one of the most widely used decentralized applications in the world.

trajectory.title: Uniswap V4 development
trajectory.description: Continued leading Uniswap Labs through the development of V4, maintaining Uniswap's position as the leading decentralized exchange on Ethereum.

name: Tems
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut EP 'For Broken Ears' in 2020 at age 25 and was featured on Wizkid's 'Essence' which peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100, earning a Grammy nomination; also featured on Drake's 'Certified Lover Boy' album in 2021.
starting_point: Born Temilade Anna Openiyi on June 11, 1995, in Lagos, Nigeria; studied economics at university and worked in digital marketing before quitting in 2018 to pursue music full-time, teaching herself production via YouTube tutorials.
current_position: Grammy-winning Nigerian singer, songwriter, and record producer; signed to RCA Records; won Best African Music Performance at the 2025 Grammys; resides in Lagos and Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Born in Lagos, Nigeria
trajectory.description: Temilade Anna Openiyi was born on June 11, 1995, in Lagos, Nigeria.

trajectory.title: Quit job to pursue music
trajectory.description: Quit her digital marketing job to pursue music full-time, teaching herself production via YouTube tutorials and releasing her self-produced debut single 'Mr Rebel' in July 2018.

trajectory.title: Breakout single 'Try Me'
trajectory.description: Released 'Try Me' in August 2019, which became her breakout hit in Nigeria and earned early critical acclaim.

trajectory.title: Debut EP 'For Broken Ears' and 'Essence' feature
trajectory.description: Released debut EP 'For Broken Ears' in September 2020; featured on Wizkid's 'Essence' which peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and earned a Grammy nomination.

trajectory.title: Featured on Drake's 'Certified Lover Boy'
trajectory.description: Featured on Drake's 'Fountains' from the 'Certified Lover Boy' album in 2021, expanding her global profile.

trajectory.title: 'Wait for U' debuts at #1 on Billboard Hot 100
trajectory.description: Her vocals from 'Higher' were sampled by Future on 'Wait for U' featuring Drake, debuting at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, making her the first African female artist to top the chart.

trajectory.title: First Grammy Award
trajectory.description: Won her first Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance for 'Wait for U' with Future and Drake; co-wrote Rihanna's 'Lift Me Up' from Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, earning Oscar and Golden Globe nominations.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Born in the Wild'
trajectory.description: Released her debut studio album 'Born in the Wild' to critical acclaim, charting internationally and embarking on a world tour.

trajectory.title: Second Grammy Award
trajectory.description: Won her second Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance for 'Love Me JeJe' at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards, becoming the first Nigerian with multiple Grammys.

name: Tyla
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with Epic Records in 2021 at age 19 following domestic success of debut single 'Getting Late'; later won the inaugural Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance in 2024 at age 22 for 'Water,' becoming the youngest African artist to win a Grammy.
starting_point: Born Tyla Laura Seethal on January 30, 2002, in Johannesburg, South Africa; grew up in the East Rand of Johannesburg; was studying mining engineering before signing with Epic Records.
current_position: Grammy-winning South African singer dubbed the 'Queen of Popiano'; two-time Grammy winner; resides between Johannesburg and Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Born in Johannesburg, South Africa
trajectory.description: Tyla Laura Seethal was born on January 30, 2002, in Johannesburg, South Africa, and grew up in the East Rand.

trajectory.title: Debut single 'Getting Late'
trajectory.description: Self-released her debut single 'Getting Late' featuring Kooldrink in late 2019 after finishing high school, achieving national success in South Africa.

trajectory.title: Signed with Epic Records
trajectory.description: Signed with Epic Records in 2021 in a joint venture with Fax Records, following the domestic success of 'Getting Late'; was studying mining engineering at the time.

trajectory.title: 'Water' goes viral globally
trajectory.description: Released 'Water' on July 28, 2023; it went viral on TikTok and entered the top ten in multiple countries including the US Billboard Hot 100, the first South African soloist to chart in 55 years.

trajectory.title: Inaugural Grammy for Best African Music Performance
trajectory.description: Won the inaugural Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance for 'Water' at the 66th Grammy Awards in February 2024, becoming the youngest African artist to win a Grammy.

trajectory.title: Self-titled debut album
trajectory.description: Released her self-titled debut album 'Tyla' in March 2024 to critical acclaim and moderate commercial success, cementing her as a global pop star.

trajectory.title: Continuing global success
trajectory.description: Released the EP 'We Wanna Party' in 2025 and announced her upcoming second studio album 'A*Pop' scheduled for release in July 2026; won her second Grammy Award.

name: Chloe Gong
milestone_by_age_26: Debut novel These Violent Delights became a New York Times bestseller in November 2020 at age 21, making her one of the youngest YA hardcover bestseller authors.
starting_point: Born on December 16, 1998, in Shanghai, China; raised in Auckland, New Zealand; began writing books at age 13 using the Notes app on her iPad; attended the University of Pennsylvania.
current_position: New York Times bestselling novelist; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2024; resides in New York City; author of multiple fantasy and science fiction novels.

trajectory.title: Born in Shanghai, China
trajectory.description: Chloe Gong was born on December 16, 1998, in Shanghai, China, and raised in Auckland, New Zealand.

trajectory.title: Began writing novels
trajectory.description: Began writing books at age 13 using the Notes app on her iPad, posting her work on Wattpad as a teenager and gaining early readers.

trajectory.title: Drafted 'These Violent Delights' and signed with agent
trajectory.description: Wrote the first draft of 'These Violent Delights' in May 2018 after her freshman year at the University of Pennsylvania; signed with literary agent Laura Crockett at age 19.

trajectory.title: NYT bestseller with 'These Violent Delights'
trajectory.description: Debut novel 'These Violent Delights' became a New York Times bestseller in November 2020, making her one of the youngest YA hardcover bestseller authors.

trajectory.title: Sequel 'Our Violent Ends' and graduation
trajectory.description: Released the sequel 'Our Violent Ends' in November 2021; graduated from the University of Pennsylvania with a double major in English and International Relations; won the Sir Julius Vogel Award for Best Youth Novel.

trajectory.title: 'Foul Lady Fortune' series
trajectory.description: Launched a new series with 'Foul Lady Fortune' in 2022, expanding her literary universe set in historical Shanghai.

trajectory.title: Forbes 30 Under 30 and 'Immortal Longings'
trajectory.description: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2024; published 'Immortal Longings,' a new adult fantasy series, further establishing her as a leading voice in young adult and fantasy fiction.

trajectory.title: Continuing literary career
trajectory.description: Continues to write and publish acclaimed fantasy and science fiction novels, with books published in over twenty countries worldwide.

name: Leila Mottley
milestone_by_age_26: Published debut novel Nightcrawling in June 2022 at age 19, which became a New York Times bestseller, an Oprah Book Club pick, and was longlisted for the Booker Prize, making her the youngest author ever nominated.
starting_point: Born in 2002/2003 in Oakland, California; named Oakland Youth Poet Laureate at age 16 in 2018; grew up in Oakland and continues to live there.
current_position: American novelist and poet; published second novel 'The Girls Who Grew Big' in June 2025; resides in Oakland, California.

trajectory.title: Born in Oakland, California
trajectory.description: Leila Mottley was born in 2002 in Oakland, California, where she was born and raised.

trajectory.title: Oakland Youth Poet Laureate
trajectory.description: Named the 2018 Oakland Youth Poet Laureate at age 16, having served as Vice Youth Poet Laureate the prior year; her poetry appeared in The New York Times.

trajectory.title: Began writing 'Nightcrawling'
trajectory.description: Began writing her debut novel 'Nightcrawling' at age 17, completing a first draft within three months during the summer after graduating high school early.

trajectory.title: 'Nightcrawling' published to acclaim
trajectory.description: Published 'Nightcrawling' in June 2022; it became a New York Times bestseller, an Oprah Book Club pick, and was longlisted for the Booker Prize, making her the youngest author ever nominated.

trajectory.title: Award recognition
trajectory.description: Won the PEN Oakland/Josephine Miles Literary Award; was a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award for Lesbian Fiction and the Audie Award for Female Narrator.

trajectory.title: Poetry collection 'woke up no light'
trajectory.description: Published her poetry collection 'woke up no light,' expanding her literary output beyond novels.

trajectory.title: Second novel 'The Girls Who Grew Big'
trajectory.description: Published her sophomore novel 'The Girls Who Grew Big' in June 2025, further establishing herself as a significant voice in contemporary American literature.

name: William Kamkwamba
milestone_by_age_26: Built an electricity-producing wind turbine from scrap materials at age 14 in 2001, and spoke at TEDGlobal at 19, leading to a bestselling memoir and global recognition by 22.
starting_point: Born on August 5, 1987, in Dowa, Malawi; grew up impoverished on a farm in the rural village of Wimbe; forced to drop out of school at 14 due to famine and inability to pay tuition.
current_position: Malawian inventor, engineer, and author; graduated from Dartmouth College; works with Moving Windmills to mentor young problem-solvers in Malawi; resides between Malawi and the US.

trajectory.title: Born in Dowa, Malawi
trajectory.description: William Kamkwamba was born on August 5, 1987, in Dowa, Malawi, to a peasant farming family as the second of seven children.

trajectory.title: Built wind turbine from scrap
trajectory.description: Built an electricity-producing wind turbine from blue gum trees, bicycle parts, and scrapyard materials at age 14, powering his family's home after being forced to drop out of school due to famine.

trajectory.title: TEDGlobal talk
trajectory.description: Invited to speak at TEDGlobal in Arusha, Tanzania, on a fellowship after his story was discovered on a blog; his moving talk about his windmill led to an outpouring of support from the TED community.

trajectory.title: Published memoir 'The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind'
trajectory.description: Published his autobiography 'The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind: Creating Currents of Electricity and Hope' with Bryan Mealer, which became a bestseller and was translated into nearly twenty languages.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at African Leadership Academy
trajectory.description: Returned to school with support from the TED community, attending the African Leadership Academy, a pan-African prep school outside Johannesburg.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Dartmouth College
trajectory.description: Graduated from Dartmouth College with a BA in Environmental Studies, having been supported through his education by the TED community and scholarships.

trajectory.title: Netflix film adaptation
trajectory.description: A Netflix film adaptation of 'The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind' directed by Chiwetel Ejiofor was released, winning the Alfred P. Sloan Prize at Sundance.

trajectory.title: Moving Windmills project
trajectory.description: Works with Moving Windmills to mentor young problem-solvers in Malawi and is developing the Moving Windmills Innovation Center in Kasungu to provide tools and mentorship for young innovators.

name: Nadya Okamoto
milestone_by_age_26: Founded PERIOD, the largest youth-run NGO in women's health, at age 16 in 2014, growing it to 800 chapters in 50 states and 40 countries by her early 20s.
starting_point: Born Nadya Teresa Okamoto on February 11, 1998, in New York; grew up in Portland, Oregon; experienced a period of homelessness as a teenager; attended Harvard College.
current_position: Content creator, entrepreneur, and author with 6M+ social media followers; co-founder and former CEO of August, a period products brand; resides in New York City.

trajectory.title: Born in New York
trajectory.description: Nadya Teresa Okamoto was born on February 11, 1998, in New York, and grew up in Portland, Oregon.

trajectory.title: Founded PERIOD (Camions of Care)
trajectory.description: Founded PERIOD, originally named Camions of Care, at age 16 in December 2014 with high school classmate Vincent Forand, inspired by conversations with homeless women about period poverty.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Harvard and ran for Cambridge City Council
trajectory.description: Moved to Cambridge to attend Harvard College in August 2016; announced her candidacy for Cambridge City Council in early 2017, the youngest candidate in the race.

trajectory.title: Hosted first Period Con
trajectory.description: Hosted the first 'Period Con,' a global conference for young activists; PERIOD had grown to hundreds of chapters across the US and internationally.

trajectory.title: Published 'Period Power'
trajectory.description: Published her debut book 'Period Power: A Manifesto for the Menstrual Movement' in October 2018; PERIOD had grown to 800 chapters in 50 states and 40 countries.

trajectory.title: Stepped down from PERIOD and co-founded August
trajectory.description: Stepped down as executive director of PERIOD in January 2020 and left the organization entirely after controversy; co-founded August, a for-profit period brand, in November 2020.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard College in June 2021; August launched as a lifestyle period brand available online and at Target, Whole Foods, and other retailers.

trajectory.title: Content creator and advocate
trajectory.description: Has grown to 6 million social media followers, creating content about building a business, mental health, and menstrual equity advocacy; continues to advocate for ending the tampon tax.

name: Marley Dias
milestone_by_age_26: Launched the #1000BlackGirlBooks campaign at age 10 in 2015, collecting over 15,000 books and becoming the youngest Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree at 13.
starting_point: Born in 2005 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; raised in West Orange, New Jersey; mother Janice Johnson Dias is co-founder of the GrassROOTS Community Foundation, which supported her campaign.
current_position: Student at Harvard University; author, activist, and producer; continues to run #1000BlackGirlBooks; serves as NEA National Ambassador for Read Across America.

trajectory.title: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
trajectory.description: Marley Emelia Dias was born in 2005 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and raised in West Orange, New Jersey.

trajectory.title: Launched #1000BlackGirlBooks
trajectory.description: Launched the #1000BlackGirlBooks campaign at age 10 in November 2015, frustrated by the lack of Black girl protagonists in her school's reading lists; collected over 9,000 books within months.

trajectory.title: Smithsonian Ingenuity Award
trajectory.description: Received the Smithsonian Ingenuity Award in the Youth Category in 2017 for her groundbreaking work on literary representation.

trajectory.title: Published first book and youngest Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Published 'Marley Dias Gets It Done: And So Can You!' with Scholastic at age 13; became the youngest person ever named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

trajectory.title: Netflix series 'Bookmarks'
trajectory.description: Became executive producer and host of the Netflix series 'Bookmarks: Celebrating Black Voices,' featuring celebrities reading books by Black authors; the series earned a 2021 NAACP Image Award nomination.

trajectory.title: Harvard freshman
trajectory.description: Enrolled at Harvard University as a freshman in 2022, continuing her advocacy for diverse books as National Ambassador for the NEA's Read Across America program.

trajectory.title: Continuing advocacy at Harvard
trajectory.description: Continues her studies at Harvard University, writing for The Harvard Crimson, and running #1000BlackGirlBooks which has collected over 15,000 books to date.

name: David Hsu
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Retool in January 2017 at age 25, went through Y Combinator's Winter 2017 batch, raised $1.5 million, and grew Retool to $2M in ARR by August 2018 at age 26, later building it to a $3.2 billion valuation.
starting_point: Born in Silicon Valley; graduated from Oxford with a double degree in computer science and philosophy; started his first company from his childhood bedroom in Palo Alto.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Retool, a software development platform valued at $3.2 billion; customers include Amazon, DoorDash, Disney, and the NFL; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Oxford
trajectory.description: Graduated from the University of Oxford with a double degree in computer science and philosophy.

trajectory.title: Founded Retool after YC pivot
trajectory.description: Entered Y Combinator's Winter 2017 batch with a UK-based Venmo competitor called Cashew; pivoted to Retool after the fintech startup was losing $1,000/day, building a platform for developers to create internal tools faster.

trajectory.title: Y Combinator Demo Day success
trajectory.description: Presented at YC Demo Day 2017, announcing they had already signed an enterprise customer pilot worth $1.5M, securing initial funding.

trajectory.title: Hacker News launch and $2M ARR
trajectory.description: Launched Retool on Hacker News on August 9, 2018, which immediately shifted the business to inbound; grew to $2M in ARR with 5-20 companies signing up daily.

trajectory.title: $3.2 billion valuation
trajectory.description: Retool reached a $3.2 billion valuation with customers including Amazon, DoorDash, Disney, Airbnb, Mercedes-Benz, and the NFL; NBC used Retool to program the Olympics.

trajectory.title: Continuing to scale Retool
trajectory.description: Continues to lead Retool as CEO, expanding into AI agents for enterprise workflows and maintaining its position as the leading internal tools platform.

name: Iyinoluwa Aboyeji
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Andela in 2014 at age 23, which received $24M Series B funding from Mark Zuckerberg in 2016, and co-founded Flutterwave in 2016 at age 25, both later becoming unicorns.
starting_point: Born Iyinoluwa Samuel Aboyeji on March 28, 1991, in Nigeria; attended Loyola Jesuit College and the University of Waterloo in Canada; grew up in Lagos.
current_position: CEO and General Partner of Future Africa, a venture platform valued at over $6 billion; co-founded two African unicorns (Andela and Flutterwave); resides in Lagos, Nigeria.

trajectory.title: Born in Nigeria
trajectory.description: Iyinoluwa Samuel Aboyeji was born on March 28, 1991, in Nigeria; raised in Lagos and educated at Loyola Jesuit College.

trajectory.title: Founded Bookneto
trajectory.description: Launched Bookneto Incorporation, a social learning platform at the University of Waterloo, which was acquired by the Canadian Innovation Center three years later.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Andela
trajectory.description: Co-founded Andela, a global job placement network for software developers, in 2014; launched first recruitment cycle in Lagos with four Nigerian engineers from over 700 applications.

trajectory.title: Andela Series A funding
trajectory.description: Andela secured $10 million in Series A funding in 2015, validating the thesis that African engineers could compete globally.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Flutterwave and Zuckerberg investment
trajectory.description: Co-founded Flutterwave, Africa's leading payments technology company, in 2016; Andela received $24M Series B funding led by Mark Zuckerberg.

trajectory.title: Left Flutterwave, started Future Africa
trajectory.description: Stepped down as Managing Director of Flutterwave in October 2018 after processing over 100 million transactions worth $2.5 billion; began building Future Africa, a venture platform.

trajectory.title: National Honour (OON)
trajectory.description: Conferred with the National Honours Award of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) by President Muhammadu Buhari on October 11, 2022.

trajectory.title: Future Africa at $6 billion valuation
trajectory.description: Leads Future Africa as CEO and General Partner, with a portfolio of 100+ companies collectively worth over $6 billion; both Andela and Flutterwave are ranked among Africa's unicorns.

name: Nodirbek Abdusattorov
milestone_by_age_26: Won the FIDE World Rapid Chess Championship in December 2021 at age 17, defeating Magnus Carlsen and Ian Nepomniachtchi to become the youngest ever World Rapid Champion.
starting_point: Born on September 18, 2004, in Tashkent, Uzbekistan; a chess prodigy who won the World Youth Chess Championships Under-8 division in 2012 at age 8.
current_position: Uzbek chess grandmaster ranked among the top five players in the world; plays for Natus Vincere; widely viewed as a potential world champion.

trajectory.title: Born in Tashkent, Uzbekistan
trajectory.description: Nodirbek Fazliddin o'g'li Abdusattorov was born on September 18, 2004, in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

trajectory.title: World Under-8 Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Under-8 division of the World Youth Chess Championships in Maribor, Slovenia, at age 8.

trajectory.title: Beat two grandmasters
trajectory.description: At age 9, defeated grandmasters Andrey Zhigalko and Rustam Khusnutdinov at the Georgy Agzamov Memorial tournament in Tashkent.

trajectory.title: Became a chess grandmaster
trajectory.description: Qualified for the grandmaster title at age 13 years, 1 month, and 11 days; FIDE awarded him the title in April 2018.

trajectory.title: Youngest World Rapid Champion
trajectory.description: Won the FIDE World Rapid Chess Championship in December 2021 at age 17, defeating Magnus Carlsen and Ian Nepomniachtchi to become the youngest ever World Rapid Champion.

trajectory.title: Olympiad gold with Uzbekistan
trajectory.description: Led Uzbekistan to a team gold medal at the 44th Chess Olympiad in Chennai, India, winning an individual silver medal on board 1.

trajectory.title: Won Prague Masters and ranked 4th in world
trajectory.description: Won the Prague Masters in 2024; was ranked fourth in the world in April 2024, establishing himself among the elite.

trajectory.title: World Blitz Championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished second at the FIDE World Blitz Chess Championship 2025, losing to Magnus Carlsen in the final, continuing to establish himself as a potential world champion.

name: Max Holloway
milestone_by_age_26: Won the interim UFC Featherweight Championship at age 25 by defeating Anthony Pettis at UFC 206 on December 10, 2016, then unified the title by beating Jose Aldo at UFC 212 on June 3, 2017.
starting_point: Born Jerome Max Keli'i Holloway on December 4, 1991, in Honolulu, Hawaii; started kickboxing at age 15 at Team Ruthless and made his UFC debut at age 20 as the youngest fighter on the roster.
current_position: Former UFC Featherweight Champion and BMF titleholder; competes in the UFC Lightweight division; considered one of the greatest featherweights of all time.

trajectory.title: Born in Honolulu, Hawaii
trajectory.description: Jerome Max Keli'i Holloway was born on December 4, 1991, in Honolulu, Hawaii.

trajectory.title: Amateur MMA and 4-0 record
trajectory.description: Started training at Team Ruthless at age 15; by 19 had amassed a 4-0 amateur/pro record and was recognized as a top featherweight prospect.

trajectory.title: UFC debut as youngest fighter on roster
trajectory.description: Made his UFC debut on February 4, 2012, at UFC 143 against Dustin Poirier as the youngest fighter on the UFC roster at age 20.

trajectory.title: Loss to Conor McGregor
trajectory.description: Lost to Conor McGregor by decision in 2013, which would be followed by a legendary 13-fight winning streak.

trajectory.title: Interim UFC Featherweight Champion
trajectory.description: Defeated Anthony Pettis at UFC 206 on December 10, 2016, to win the interim UFC Featherweight Championship.

trajectory.title: Unified UFC Featherweight title
trajectory.description: Stopped Jose Aldo at UFC 212 on June 3, 2017, to unify the UFC Featherweight Championship, beginning a dominant reign as champion.

trajectory.title: Title defenses against Aldo and Ortega
trajectory.description: Defended the featherweight title with stoppages of Jose Aldo at UFC 218 and Brian Ortega at UFC 231, establishing himself as the dominant featherweight.

trajectory.title: Lost title to Volkanovski
trajectory.description: Lost the UFC featherweight title to Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 245 in December 2019, ending his championship reign.

trajectory.title: Won BMF title with iconic knockout
trajectory.description: Knocked out Justin Gaethje at 4:59 of the fifth round at UFC 300 to win the BMF title, one of the most iconic moments in UFC history.

trajectory.title: Moved to welterweight
trajectory.description: Made his welterweight debut in 2026, continuing his career across multiple weight classes as one of the most beloved fighters in UFC history.

name: David Benavidez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC super middleweight world title at age 20 in September 2017, becoming the youngest super middleweight champion in boxing history.
starting_point: Born Anthony David Benavidez on December 17, 1996, in Phoenix, Arizona, to a Mexican father and Ecuadorian mother; began training in the gym at age 3 with his father José Benavidez Sr.; struggled with obesity as a teenager, weighing 250 pounds at 13 before losing over 100 pounds.
current_position: Three-division world champion; holds unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight titles and WBC light heavyweight title; nicknamed 'The Mexican Monster'; professional record of 30-0.

trajectory.title: Born in Phoenix, Arizona
trajectory.description: Anthony David Benavidez was born on December 17, 1996, in Phoenix, Arizona, to a Mexican father and Ecuadorian mother.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut at age 16, defeating Erasmo Moreno by knockout in one round in Puerto Peñasco, Mexico.

trajectory.title: Signed with Sampson Boxing
trajectory.description: Signed a promotional deal with Sampson Lewkowicz's Sampson Boxing in October 2015; had a record of 12 wins with 11 stoppages by year's end.

trajectory.title: Youngest super middleweight champion
trajectory.description: Defeated Ronald Gavril via split decision on September 8, 2017, to win the WBC super middleweight world title at age 20, becoming the youngest super middleweight champion in history.

trajectory.title: Regained WBC super middleweight title
trajectory.description: After being stripped of the title, regained the WBC super middleweight championship by knocking out Anthony Dirrell in September 2019.

trajectory.title: Wins over Plant and Andrade
trajectory.description: Defeated Caleb Plant in March 2023 and Demetrius Andrade in November 2023 in dominant fashion, solidifying his reputation as 'The Mexican Monster.'

trajectory.title: Moved to light heavyweight
trajectory.description: Defeated Oleksandr Gvozdyk in June 2024 to become interim WBC light heavyweight champion, making the jump from super middleweight.

trajectory.title: WBC light heavyweight champion
trajectory.description: Became the WBC light heavyweight champion in 2025 after defeating David Morrell Jr. and being elevated when Dmitry Bivol vacated the title.

trajectory.title: Unified cruiserweight champion
trajectory.description: Won the unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight titles in May 2026, becoming a three-division world champion.

name: Letsile Tebogo
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 200m at age 21 at the 2024 Paris Olympics, earning Botswana's first-ever Olympic gold medal, and won silver in the 100m at the 2023 World Championships at age 20.
starting_point: Born on June 7, 2003, in Kanye, Botswana, a village 83 kilometers southwest of the capital Gaborone; grew up playing football and sprinting, focusing on track after football injuries.
current_position: Olympic gold medalist and Botswana's first-ever Olympic champion; sponsored by Nike; ranked #2 in the world in the 200m; resides in Botswana.

trajectory.title: Born in Kanye, Botswana
trajectory.description: Letsile Tebogo was born on June 7, 2003, in Kanye, Botswana, a village 83 kilometers southwest of Gaborone.

trajectory.title: Began taking sprinting seriously
trajectory.description: Began focusing seriously on track after injuries hampered his football career, encouraged by his teachers.

trajectory.title: World U20 Championships 100m gold
trajectory.description: Won the 100m gold at the 2021 World Athletics Under-20 Championships in Nairobi, becoming the first Botswana athlete to claim the 100m title at any World Championships level.

trajectory.title: World U20 100m record
trajectory.description: Set a new world under-20 100m record of 9.96 seconds at the Gaborone International Meet, becoming the first man from Botswana to break the 10-second barrier.

trajectory.title: World Championships silver and bronze
trajectory.description: Won silver in the 100m and bronze in the 200m at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, becoming Africa's first world 100m medallist in athletics.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold in 200m
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in the 200m at the 2024 Paris Olympics in 19.46 seconds, earning Botswana's first-ever Olympic gold medal and becoming the first African to win the Olympic 200m.

trajectory.title: Olympic 4x400m relay silver
trajectory.description: Won a silver medal in the 4x400m relay at the 2024 Paris Olympics just two days after his 200m gold, serving as Botswana's flagbearer at both ceremonies.

trajectory.title: Continuing sprint career
trajectory.description: Continues as one of the world's leading sprinters, ranked #2 in the 200m, inspiring a new generation of African athletes to challenge Jamaican and American dominance in sprinting.

name: Alexis Barreyat
milestone_by_age_26: Founded and launched BeReal, a photo-sharing social app, in early 2020 at age 24, which later reached #1 on Apple's App Store and was named iPhone App of the Year 2022.
