starting_point: Born in France; attended 42 coding school in Paris from 2013 to 2016; worked in media production at GoPro in Munich from 2016 to 2018 before founding BeReal.
current_position: Former founder and CEO of BeReal; stepped down as CEO after BeReal was acquired by Voodoo in June 2024 for a reported €500 million.

trajectory.title: Attended 42 coding school
trajectory.description: Attended 42 (born2code), a tuition-free coding school in Paris, from July 2013 to March 2016, learning software development.

trajectory.title: Joined GoPro in media production
trajectory.description: Worked in media production at GoPro in Munich from March 2016 to December 2018, gaining experience in content and media.

trajectory.title: Began developing BeReal
trajectory.description: Began working on BeReal with co-founder Kévin Perreau in late 2019, creating a social media app focused on authentic, unpolished photos.

trajectory.title: Launched BeReal
trajectory.description: Launched BeReal on the App Store in early 2020; the app prompts users to post photos of themselves at randomly assigned times, a rebellion against curated social media.

trajectory.title: Gained traction on French college campuses
trajectory.description: BeReal slowly gained traction in 2021 across French college campuses, reaching 500K users through a college ambassador program.

trajectory.title: BeReal goes viral globally
trajectory.description: BeReal went viral in 2022, expanding into the UK and US markets; reached over 10 million daily active users by August 2022; named iPhone App of the Year 2022.

trajectory.title: Raised $60M at $600M valuation
trajectory.description: Raised $60 million in funding at a $600 million valuation; larger rivals like Instagram and TikTok launched similar features in response.

trajectory.title: BeReal acquired by Voodoo
trajectory.description: BeReal was acquired by French gaming company Voodoo in June 2024 for a reported €500 million; Barreyat stepped down as CEO, replaced by Aymeric Roffé.

name: Shane Curran
milestone_by_age_26: Won the BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition in January 2017 at age 16 for qCrypt quantum-secure encryption, was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2018 at 17, and founded Evervault in 2018-2019 at age 18-19, raising $3.2M seed from Sequoia Capital by October 2019.
starting_point: Born in 2000 in Dublin, Ireland; learned to code at age 7 and started his first company at 12; attended Terenure College in Dublin.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Evervault, a Dublin-based encryption infrastructure company backed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, and Index Ventures.

trajectory.title: Born in Dublin, Ireland
trajectory.description: Shane Curran was born in 2000 in Dublin, Ireland.

trajectory.title: Learned to code
trajectory.description: Learned to code at age 7, beginning a path that would lead to early entrepreneurship and technical innovation.

trajectory.title: Started first company
trajectory.description: Started his first company at age 12, becoming one of the youngest programmers to approach tech media in Ireland.

trajectory.title: Won BT Young Scientist for qCrypt
trajectory.description: Won the 53rd BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition in January 2017 for 'qCrypt,' a quantum-secure encrypted data storage platform, representing Ireland at the EU Contest for Young Scientists.

trajectory.title: Forbes 30 Under 30 and founded Evervault
trajectory.description: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in January 2018; founded Evervault in 2018 after briefly beginning a business and law degree at University College Dublin, which he dropped out of after three days.

trajectory.title: $3.2M seed from Sequoia Capital
trajectory.description: Announced a $3.2 million seed round led by Sequoia Capital in October 2019, with participation from Kleiner Perkins and Frontline Ventures.

trajectory.title: $16M Series A from Index Ventures
trajectory.description: Closed a $16 million Series A investment round led by Index Ventures in May 2020, with participation from Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, and angel investors including Dylan Field.

trajectory.title: Continuing to lead Evervault
trajectory.description: Continues to lead Evervault as CEO, building encryption infrastructure for developers from the company's Dublin headquarters.

name: Joey Krug
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Augur, one of the first decentralized prediction market protocols on Ethereum, in 2014 at age 19, and organized the first ICO on Ethereum in 2015, raising $5.7 million at age 20.
starting_point: Born in Knoxville, Illinois; started programming in Applesoft BASIC in middle school after his father bought him an Apple II GS; studied computer science at Pomona College before dropping out to pursue crypto.
current_position: Partner at Founders Fund focused on crypto strategy; co-founder of Augur and Eco; formerly co-CIO at Pantera Capital; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Started Bitcoin mining
trajectory.description: Started exploring Bitcoin mining in 2011 while building vintage hardware with his father, beginning his crypto journey.

trajectory.title: Built Bitcoin POS system and started college
trajectory.description: Built a Bitcoin point-of-sale payment system in 2013; began studying computer science at Pomona College but did not complete his degree.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Augur
trajectory.description: Co-founded the Forecast Foundation, the organization behind Augur, a decentralized prediction market protocol built on Ethereum, at age 19.

trajectory.title: First ICO on Ethereum
trajectory.description: Organized the first ICO on Ethereum in 2015, raising $5.7 million for Augur, a peer-to-peer betting platform, at age 20.

trajectory.title: Joined Pantera Capital as co-CIO
trajectory.description: Joined Pantera Capital, one of the largest blockchain-focused investment firms, as co-chief investment officer, managing hundreds of millions across crypto funds.

trajectory.title: Joined Founders Fund as Partner
trajectory.description: Joined Peter Thiel's Founders Fund as a Partner in April 2023, focused on defining the next decade of Founders Fund's crypto strategy.

trajectory.title: Leading crypto investments at Founders Fund
trajectory.description: Continues as Partner at Founders Fund, backing the next wave of generational crypto startups and founders, including Polymarket.

name: Blake Resnick
milestone_by_age_26: Founded BRINC Drones in 2019 at age 18 (initial work began at 17 in 2017), received a Thiel Fellowship in 2020, was named the youngest honoree on Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2022, and raised a $25 million Series A in 2021 at age 21, building a drone company valued at $300 million by 2023.
starting_point: Born in Las Vegas, Nevada; started college at 14 at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and built a fusion reactor in his garage; interned at McLaren, Tesla, and DJI before dropping out of Northwestern University at 17.
current_position: Founder and CEO of BRINC Drones, a tactical drone company valued at $300 million; based in Seattle, Washington; serves over 400 customers including police departments worldwide.

trajectory.title: Born in Las Vegas, Nevada
trajectory.description: Blake Resnick was born in Las Vegas, Nevada; started college at 14 at UNLV and built a fusion reactor in his garage.

trajectory.title: Started college and built fusion reactor
trajectory.description: Started college at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas at age 14 and built an inertial electrostatic confinement nuclear fusion reactor in his garage.

trajectory.title: Internships at McLaren, Tesla, and DJI
trajectory.description: Interned at McLaren developing a brake cooling system, at Tesla creating a predictive model for CAN bus latency, and at DJI designing a drone tether system.

trajectory.title: Founded BRINC after Las Vegas shooting
trajectory.description: Inspired by the deadliest mass shooting in American history on the Las Vegas Strip in October 2017, dropped out of Northwestern and founded BRINC to build drones for first responders.

trajectory.title: Officially founded BRINC Drones
trajectory.description: Officially founded BRINC Drones in 2019, working with the Las Vegas SWAT unit to develop the first BRINC drone design for public safety operations.

trajectory.title: Thiel Fellowship and Sam Altman investment
trajectory.description: Received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2020; Sam Altman became BRINC's first external investor, taking the entire $2.25 million seed round.

trajectory.title: $25M Series A
trajectory.description: Raised a $25 million Series A in 2021, expanding BRINC's scope across public safety verticals with drones used in Ukraine and by police departments.

trajectory.title: Youngest Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree
trajectory.description: Named the youngest honoree on Forbes 30 Under 30 in the social impact category; moved BRINC headquarters from Las Vegas to Seattle.

trajectory.title: $300M valuation
trajectory.description: BRINC reached a valuation of $300 million as of April 2023, with Resnick's personal stake making him worth over $100 million at age 23.

trajectory.title: Continuing to scale BRINC
trajectory.description: Continues to lead BRINC Drones with nearly 100 employees and over 400 customers, building life-saving technology for first responders globally.

name: Awais Ahmed
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pixxel Space Technologies in February 2019 at age 20-21, building India's first private hyperspectral satellite company, and was named to Fortune India 40 Under 40 in 2022 at age 23-24, with Pixxel launching its first satellites and securing a NASA contract.
starting_point: Born in Aldur, Chikmagalur district, India; didn't have internet access until 8th grade; father ran a pharmacy and bought him science books; attended BITS Pilani for mathematics and manufacturing engineering.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Pixxel Space Technologies, based in Bengaluru and Los Angeles; Pixxel is the first Indian space startup to secure a NASA contract; company valued with $95M+ in total funding.

trajectory.title: Born in Aldur, India
trajectory.description: Awais Ahmed was born in Aldur, Chikmagalur district, India, a village 5 hours from Bengaluru; didn't have internet access until 8th grade.

trajectory.title: Founding team of Hyperloop India
trajectory.description: Became a founding member and engineering lead at Hyperloop India, one of 20 finalist teams in the SpaceX Hyperloop pod competition, while at BITS Pilani.

trajectory.title: Student satellite team with ISRO
trajectory.description: Worked on a student satellite project with ISRO (India's space agency) as part of Team Anant at BITS Pilani, gaining hands-on satellite engineering experience.

trajectory.title: Founded Pixxel Space Technologies
trajectory.description: Co-founded Pixxel in February 2019 while still in his final year at BITS Pilani, building India's first private hyperspectral satellite company.

trajectory.title: First satellite launch and Series A
trajectory.description: Pixxel launched its first hyperspectral imaging satellite 'Shakuntala' in April 2022 from Cape Canaveral, India's first private commercial imaging satellite; secured $27M Series A.

trajectory.title: Named to Fortune India 40 Under 40
trajectory.description: Named to Fortune India 40 Under 40 in 2022, recognized as among the leading young entrepreneurs in India's private space sector.

trajectory.title: NASA contract and NRO contract
trajectory.description: Pixxel secured a five-year contract from the National Reconnaissance Office of the US in March 2023, and had already secured a NASA contract for hyperspectral Earth-observation data.

trajectory.title: Scaling Pixxel globally
trajectory.description: Continues to lead Pixxel with 200-300 employees and $95M+ in total funding, building the Firefly hyperspectral constellation and Aurora cloud-based data platform.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Kalshi in 2018 at age 22 with Tarek Mansour, entered Y Combinator's Winter 2019 batch, and built the first federally regulated prediction market exchange in the United States, later becoming the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire at age 29.
starting_point: Born in Brazil; trained in ballet before studying at MIT where she earned a Bachelor's in Computer Science and Mathematics and a Master's of Engineering; worked at Bridgewater, Citadel, and Five Rings Capital before founding Kalshi.
current_position: Co-founder and COO of Kalshi, the first federally regulated prediction market exchange in the US; world's youngest self-made woman billionaire at age 29; resides in New York.

trajectory.title: Born in Brazil
trajectory.description: Luana Lopes Lara was born in Brazil and trained in ballet before pursuing a career in mathematics and technology.

trajectory.title: Internships at Bridgewater and Citadel
trajectory.description: Gained experience at elite financial institutions including Bridgewater, Citadel, and Five Rings Capital while studying at MIT.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Kalshi
trajectory.description: Co-founded Kalshi with MIT classmate Tarek Mansour in 2018, building the first federally regulated prediction market exchange in the United States.

trajectory.title: Y Combinator Winter 2019 batch
trajectory.description: Entered Y Combinator's Winter 2019 batch, securing initial funding and mentorship to build the prediction market platform.

trajectory.title: Years of regulatory battles
trajectory.description: Spent years pursuing regulatory approvals for Kalshi, facing skepticism from government agencies and even their own board, with many telling them it was impossible.

trajectory.title: Kalshi receives CFTC approval
trajectory.description: Kalshi received regulatory approval from the CFTC to operate as a federally regulated prediction market exchange, a landmark achievement after years of persistence.

trajectory.title: Kalshi gains mainstream traction
trajectory.description: Kalshi gained mainstream attention during the 2024 US election cycle, allowing users to trade contracts on real-world outcomes including elections, weather, and pop culture.

trajectory.title: World's youngest self-made woman billionaire
trajectory.description: Became the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire at age 29 as Kalshi's valuation soared, featured on Forbes 30 Under 30 and named a CNBC Changemaker.

name: Ye Shiwen
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals at age 16 at the 2012 London Olympics, breaking the world record in the 400m individual medley and the Olympic record in the 200m individual medley.
starting_point: Born on March 1, 1996, in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China; parents were amateur athletes (father a runner, mother a long jump champion); started swimming at age 6 after a kindergarten teacher noticed her large hands and feet.
current_position: Chinese competitive swimmer; competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics; continues to swim professionally for China.

trajectory.title: Born in Hangzhou, China
trajectory.description: Ye Shiwen was born on March 1, 1996, in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, to parents who were both amateur athletes.

trajectory.title: Started swimming
trajectory.description: Began swimming at age 6 after her kindergarten teacher noticed her large hands and feet, enrolling at the Chen Jinglun Sport School.

trajectory.title: Joined Chinese national team
trajectory.description: Joined the Chinese national junior training camp in October 2008, beginning her rise through the competitive swimming ranks.

trajectory.title: Asian Games double gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in both the 200m and 400m individual medley at the 2010 Asian Games in Guangzhou at age 14, announcing herself on the international stage.

trajectory.title: World Championship gold in 200m IM
trajectory.description: Won the 200m individual medley title at the 2011 World Championships in Shanghai, defeating reigning world champion Arianna Kukors.

trajectory.title: Double Olympic gold at London 2012
trajectory.description: Won two Olympic gold medals at the 2012 London Olympics at age 16, breaking the world record in the 400m IM (4:28.43) and the Olympic record in the 200m IM (2:07.57).

trajectory.title: Disappointing Rio Olympics
trajectory.description: Finished eighth in the 200m IM and 27th in the 400m IM at the 2016 Rio Olympics, failing to win any medals as her times slipped.

trajectory.title: World Championship silver medals
trajectory.description: Won silver medals in both the 200m and 400m IM at the 2019 World Championships in Gwangju, finishing behind Katinka Hosszu, marking a career resurgence.

trajectory.title: Competed at Paris Olympics
trajectory.description: Competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, finishing sixth in the 200m breaststroke and tenth in the 200m IM, continuing her long international career.
